I will start from what worked for me last year and only adjust a little. On my 10.1 mu, I will keep the wheat-maize rotation as the main part because that is steady and I know how to manage it. I will put 8.0 mu into wheat-maize and leave 2.1 mu for chili, because chili can bring cash but it needs more labor, more spraying, and more careful watering. My family has some people working outside, so I cannot spread myself too thin. I do have well irrigation, so I am not too scared of dry spells, but electricity, fertilizer, seed, and pesticide all cost money, so I count every bag.

For wheat, I will use improved seed, not old saved seed, because the better wheat stands more even and neighbors who used it had better heads. I will not cut fertilizer too hard. If I save 20 or 30 yuan on fertilizer and lose yield, that loss is bigger. I will give wheat enough base fertilizer and then topdress nitrogen at jointing. For maize, I will use hybrid seed like I usually do. Hybrid maize costs more, but the ears are better and more uniform. I will feed maize a bit heavier on nitrogen because if maize goes hungry in the fast-growing stage, yield drops quickly. For chili, I will not farm it the rough way. Chili needs more phosphorus and potassium than grain, and I will spray more times because once disease or thrips get ahead of me, the field becomes hard to hold. I will still stay close to what I have seen work around me. I do not like gambling on big changes.
